headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing can expose uploaded documents, while Taipy has no documented isolation or data-handling controls in the profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity can browse live web content and analyze uploaded documents, so malicious text could be surfaced in its outputs. Taipy has no documented input-parsing or shared-channel surface, and no direct bridge is shown. The pairwise pathway is therefore possible but appears to require manual transfer or unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF Perplexity outputs are manually copied into Taipy inputs, prompt-like instructions in the content can influence downstream processing.
IF an external orchestrator bridges Perplexity browsing output into Taipy without provenance filtering, injection risk increases.
mitigations: Strip instructions from copied text before passing it onward.
Use a fixed schema for Taipy inputs instead of free-form text.
Add a provenance label to all Perplexity-derived content.
Review any copied web excerpts before ingestion.
requires-engineering: implement content sanitization at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and explicitly handles uploaded PDFs/images plus browsing context, so sensitive content can leave the local environment. Taipy’s profile shows no network egress and no data classes touched, but the pair still creates a leakage path if Perplexity is used on sensitive files that are then fed into Taipy workflows. The interaction is plausible in default use, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF uploaded documents contain sensitive data and are sent to Perplexity, that data is processed by a vendor-hosted service.
IF Taipy workflows ingest Perplexity-derived summaries, sensitive content can propagate into downstream artifacts.
mitigations: Avoid uploading sensitive documents to Perplexity.
Redact identifiers before analysis.
Keep Taipy inputs limited to non-sensitive summaries.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workflows.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks at the Perplexity-to-Taipy boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Perplexity has no filesystem write, shell, or git modification capability, while Taipy only shows no network egress and no explicit write surface. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible overlap is indirect coordination through shared user-managed artifacts, so the blast radius is small and the pathway is not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external artifact through a separate orchestrator, they may contend indirectly.
IF Taipy is extended with write-capable plugins outside this profile, conflict risk rises.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same file.
Use a single writer for shared artifacts.
Lock files before downstream processing.
requires-engineering: add explicit concurrency control in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers from browsing, and Taipy is a data-engineering/automation tool that may consume upstream outputs. If Taipy treats Perplexity’s text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream transformations or automation. Taipy’s profile does not show verification safeguards, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Taipy ingests Perplexity-generated text without validation, incorrect claims can propagate.
IF Taipy automates actions from those claims, the impact expands beyond a single document.
mitigations: Require human review before Taipy acts on Perplexity output.
Validate key fields against source data.
Use confidence thresholds for automated steps.
Log provenance for every imported claim.
requires-engineering: add verification gates in Taipy pipelines.

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity’s profile shows vendor-hosted processing of uploaded documents and browsing context, while Taipy’s profile provides no residency, retention, or certification details. That mismatch creates a compliance uncertainty for regulated data classes, especially if the pair is used on sensitive documents. The other agent is not cited for a specific residency violation because its compliance posture is undocumented.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded to Perplexity, vendor-hosted processing may conflict with local policy.
IF Taipy stores or transforms the same regulated data without documented retention controls, compliance gaps widen.
mitigations: Do not use regulated data in the pair until policies are confirmed.
Review vendor privacy and retention terms.
Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Keep audit logs of all transfers.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for the workflow.
